notes.text: The upper block gives the source’s definition of beta: a group of compatible pairs (g, bar g), pi = Aut(tilde Pi/Pi), a projection to G and an object set Ob tilde Pi with an evident action. The arrow/shaft diagram is transcribed as ink, without a proof of exactness. The separate phrase Variantes profinies… follows.

Circled paragraph 8 recalls an extension and a nonempty set on which pi acts freely, then places a double-headed correspondence next to the groupoid tuple. It proposes interpreting data called a triple. The small inserted chi makes the written tuple contain four entries; the word triple is retained without correction.

The source asks whether T is isomorphic to the hatted integer group, with an explicit question mark. It adds chi : G to Aut(T), and a crowded comparison involving hatted Z-star and canon.?. The tall curved stroke after Z-star is now explicitly represented as an unsure closing-parenthesis/question-like sign; the whole parenthesis remains unsure. No canonical identification is asserted by this review.

A separate chi-colon is visibly interlinear above où. It is retained at that position independently of the complete chi map below; the source provides no caret settling its intended grammatical attachment. Phi maps the round-labelled set to Hom_gr(T, pi). The last line ends mid-parenthesis at opérant; no completion is supplied.

The bottom-left 18 is in pencil and is assigned to an unnamed hand. H’s long editorial notation note is not source text. Small detached pen taps and paper marks without a legible textual form are not promoted to superscripts, punctuation, or cancelled words.

The two final tuple components are compressed a graphs with a low shoulder and flattened return. Main compared both with the explicitly named action map on017 and with018; the preferred reading is now a. The round set label remains tau/calligraphic T, and the rounded group glyph retains its shared E/Sigma alternative. These alphabet identifications do not assert different mathematical objects.

Both final tuple components are now a at medium confidence after checking their actual shoulders and flattened returns against the current shared notation. Unlike an a-first uncertainty wrapper, accepted sim-first on this page changes its provisional preferred reading. Both findings therefore have certainty_only=false and revise the existing material rows to against_C=false/against_H=true. No duplicate locus is added to the aggregate.

The object-action continuation has two dark dots and two lighter elongated strokes. The candidate preserves all four shapes and their ascending placement in inline TikZ instead of normalizing them to four equal periods. The separate Variantes profinies suspension remains three physical marks.

The lower extension’s last two connectors are drawn from their visible strokes. Long converging/retraced segments are retained at the rounded-group-to-G link; the G-to-1 link has a small open two-tine return whose semantic direction is not asserted. The first two links remain bare. The detached tap above the first shaft is not a secure label.

The small tuple chi-comma, the isolated chi-colon above où and the full chi map below remain separate insertions. Their crops show no independent insertion caret or guide to add. The crossing after T is not a canceled word; Phi’s loop flourish is not assigned an attachment function.

The one original MARKS decision M0698 remains undecided with the extra curved sign after Z-star explicitly preserved. Five pre-existing doubts remain after the two tuple doubts are removed. No new MARKS identifier or replacement of an uncertain source question by a mathematical assertion is introduced.
